question: An operations team is agreeing which Claude-assisted outputs must be reviewed by a person before use. Which two situations clearly require that review? Select two.
options: A) A first draft of brainstorming prompts to be discussed at a team workshop later.
B) A set of notes summarising an internal retrospective for the team that attended it.
C) A rewritten meeting agenda that the chair will read through before the meeting.
D) A customer-facing notice that will be published under the organisation's own name.
E) A written assessment feeding into a decision about an employee's contract.
correct_answers: D) A customer-facing notice that will be published under the organisation's own name.
E) A written assessment feeding into a decision about an employee's contract.
explanations: Discussion material is reviewed by definition when the workshop happens, and nothing is acted on before people have looked at it together.
Notes for the people who were in the room are low stakes and self-correcting, because those readers can immediately spot anything that is wrong.
The chair reading the agenda before the meeting already supplies the review, and an error in it is trivially correctable on the spot.
Correct. External publication under the organisation's name is hard to withdraw and carries reputational consequences, so a person must own it before it is released.
Correct. This is a different trigger from publication: decisions affecting a person's employment must be made and owned by a human regardless of how good the draft is.
